Those directive lines sit *inside* Rust comments (via the `/* /* */` divergence) so Rust never parses the `#`, while C++ treats them as real preprocessor directives and skips the Rust code.\n\n**What each compiler actually sees:**\n- **Rust** → just lines 19–30 (`fn main() { … }`); everything else is comment.\n- **C++** → just lines 2–14 (includes + `int main`); the Rust block is `#if 0`-skipped.\n\n### Design"}}

I hit and fixed exactly this during testing.\n\n**Hiding Rust from C++**: lines 17 & 32 use `#if 0` / `#endif`. Those directive lines sit *inside* Rust comments (via the `/* /* */` divergence) so Rust never parses the `#`, while C++ treats them as real preprocessor directives and skips the Rust code.\n\n**What each compiler actually sees:**\n- **Rust** → just lines 19–30 (`fn main() { … }`); everything else is comment.\n- **C++** → just lines 2–14 (includes + `int main`); the Rust block is `#if 0`-skipped.\n\n### Design notes"}}
